newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cathay's Eddington declines comment on Ansett.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cathay's Eddington declines comment on Ansett.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd managing director Rod Eddington declined on Wednesday to comment on industry and media speculation that he would soon become chief executive of domestic and international carrier Ansett Australia.
Asked if the speculation was correct, Eddington said: "No comment. It (Cathay) is a publicly listed company and I can't (comment)."
Eddington, who is visiting Australia as part of a Hong Kong trade delegation headed by Chief Secretary Anson Chan, is to address a Hong Kong-Australia business forum here on Thursday.
Earlier, a source close to Ansett told Reuters that Eddington would join Ansett as its new chief executive early next year.

The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported in May that Eddington was considering the position after Cathay's parent, the Swire Pacific group, sold to below 50 percent of the airline and a Beijing-linked company increased its stake.

Eddington, who was born in Australia, was understood to have been waiting for the completion of TNT Ltd's sale of its 50 percent Ansett stake to Air New Zealand before making a final decision on the position, the Herald said.
The Australian government gave final approval to the deal last week. Media group News Corp hold the remaining 50 percent of Ansett. -- Melbourne bureau 613-9286-1421
